name: Hyperframes
role: HTML-to-MP4 renderer seeking a paused timeline in headless Chrome; reference, not a VCR dependency
summary: HeyGen's open-source framework that renders HTML compositions (data-attribute timing, tracks, sub-compositions) to deterministic MP4 by seeking each frame in headless Chrome. Supports GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js and WAAPI. CLI: init, preview, render; Docker and AWS Lambda for scale. Needs Node 22+ and FFmpeg. Per ADR 0001 it is a reference for VCR's own engine, not a dependency.
use_when: Need a finished browser-authored video today, outside VCR's own pipeline
Studying a working seek-and-capture timeline contract, tracks and registry as reference for VCR
Captioned or music-synced HTML video where its ~450-block registry saves hand-building
avoid_when: Native sources (Blender, Manim) or filtergraph compositing: FFmpeg, no HTML round trip
Inside VCR proper: ADR 0001 builds the compositor in-house; Playwright plus FFmpeg for capture
Alpha PNG layers for a later compositor: Playwright seek-and-screenshot capture, not an MP4 render
license: Apache-2.0; README states no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds
notes: Moved from A9 to A5: it is a working HTML-to-video renderer, not a candidate.
Not a VCR dependency per ADR 0001 (in-house composition engine). Reference and inspiration only.

2026-10-26: earlier record said 'HeyGen terms; plan usage limits apply'; the repository README says Apache-2.0 with no render fees, while hosted HeyGen services may have plans. Not reconciled beyond the README.
2026-10-26: the install check uses npx, which downloads the package on first use.

assessment.rationale: Apache-2.0 repo with release v0.8.203 published 2026-10-26 and a push the same day; very active, pre-1.0 so API churn is likely. Kept as reference per ADR 0001; reach for it as a standalone renderer when a browser-authored video is needed now.
